issues.legal_issue: A subsequent suit for possession based on title is not barred by the rule against splitting claims when its cause of action differs from that of the earlier suit and the earlier cause of action did not permit the relief sought in the subsequent suit.
material_facts: The earlier suit sought a declaration that the plaintiff was entitled to be impleaded as the deceased owner's legal representative in execution proceedings and to continue those proceedings.
The earlier suit arose from the dismissal of the plaintiff's application to be impleaded in the execution proceedings.
The subsequent suit sought possession of the disputed lands on the basis of the plaintiff's title.
The relief sought in the subsequent suit could not have been claimed in the earlier suit.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent suit for possession of the lands was not barred by Order 2, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Order 2, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires a plaintiff to include the whole claim available in respect of the cause of action on which the suit is brought. A cause of action is the foundation of the suit; if it permits a wider relief than the plaintiff claims, the plaintiff cannot later seek the balance in an independent proceeding. But the rule does not bar a later suit where the earlier cause of action did not form the foundation of the later suit and could not support the relief sought in it. The Court relied on Mohd. Hafiz v. Mohd. Zakaria, [1922] L.R. 49 I.A. 9.

predicates.subsequent_suit_for_possession_on_title: The plaintiff brought a later suit seeking possession of property on the basis of title.
predicates.earlier_suit_based_on_distinct_cause: The plaintiff's earlier suit arose from a different event and sought relief concerning participation in execution proceedings.
predicates.earlier_cause_did_not_permit_later_relie: The cause of action underlying the earlier suit did not enable the plaintiff to claim the possession relief sought in the later suit.

issues.definition: When a later title-based possession suit follows an earlier suit founded on a distinct cause that did not permit the later relief, the later claim is not barred by the rule against splitting claims.

issues.legal_issue: Mesne profits cannot be awarded in an appeal when no claim for them was made in the plaint.
material_facts: The appellant asked the Court to award mesne profits from the date of the suit.
The plaint contained no claim for mesne profits.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not award mesne profits in the appeal and stated that any claim for them had to be pursued separately according to law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court cannot consider awarding mesne profits in the appeal when the plaint made no claim for them; any entitlement must be pursued through separate steps according to law.

predicates.appeal_seeking_mesne_profits: A party asked the appellate court to award mesne profits.
predicates.mesne_profits_not_claimed_in_plaint: The plaintiff did not seek mesne profits in the plaint.

issues.definition: When an appeal seeks mesne profits that were not claimed in the plaint, mesne profits are not awarded in that appeal.
